content_html:
Neural “Programming Language” - Spike-Code Stack

If Neurons Had a Programming Language

Neurons do not use a formal, symbolic language like Python. But the brain does communicate in a layered spike code: spikes are the tokens; rate/temporal/population codes provide semantics; circuit motifs and dynamics act like grammar and control flow; synaptic plasticity compiles experience into connection weights.

Brain Stack ↔ Programming Concepts

Brain layer Neuroscience examples Programming analogy
Tokens Spikes (all-or-none), EPSPs/IPSPs, spike trains Bits, instruction words, opcodes
Semantics Rate coding; temporal coding (phase-of-oscillation, latency); population/sparse codes Data types & encodings; serialization
Grammar Feedforward/feedback circuits; oscillatory coupling; attractor dynamics Control flow (if/for/while), modules, message passing
Compilation Hebbian learning, STDP; neuromodulators (dopamine) gating plasticity Compiler/linker output; configuration; runtime flags
Execution Distributed, asynchronous network dynamics Parallel runtime; event loop; actor systems

  4. Plasticity rules (Hebbian, STDP) & neuromodulation — Bi & Poo (1998): Synaptic modifications; STDP; Schultz (1997): Dopamine & reward prediction.
